elementDynamiek.Lucht-Vuur: Ideal checkout match: {naamB} gives {naamA} oxygen and a plan, {naamA} gives {naamB} action and fireworks. The only charge is that you're still debating at 03:00 a decision that should have been made hours ago.
elementDynamiek.Vuur-Water: {naamA} lights the flame, {naamB} puts it out with a monologue about feelings that should also have been printed. Steam appears — and steam isn't bad, but it always leaves a watermark on the receipt.

elementDynamiek.Aarde-Water: The classic builder-and-provider combo: {naamA} puts up the house, {naamB} makes it a home. The receipt is one shared expense that rarely causes a fight — as long as the dishwasher is loaded correctly.
elementDynamiek.Lucht-Lucht: A conversation that never ends, a plan that never starts: {naamA} and {naamB} think eight years ahead together and don't move a chair. The checkout loves this duo — an awful lot gets decided about what you're not buying.
elementDynamiek.Lucht-Water: {naamA} philosophises aloud about the meaning of life; {naamB} immediately has to cry about it. Not a bad pair, but the receipt is full of 'discussed, not decided' — luckily fog often clears during a long conversation.
elementDynamiek.Water-Water: Two Water signs together are a periodic emotional tsunami: {naamA} and {naamB} feel the same thing at the same moment and process it each in their own way. The receipt reads like a novel in which you're both the author and the main character.

tags.boogschutter-boogschutter: Two identical flights to the same place, and both of them back again — separately.
tags.boogschutter-kreeft: One books the flight, the other the home base. Works as long as the luggage can come along.
tags.boogschutter-leeuw: Two fireworks factories in one show garden: audience guaranteed, fire extinguisher forgotten.
tags.boogschutter-maagd: One says yes to everything, the other notes why that will go wrong. This is going to be a great episode.
tags.boogschutter-ram: Two drivers and one handbrake — which neither of them will ever touch.
tags.boogschutter-schorpioen: Blunt honesty versus deep concealment. The honesty clashes; the attraction clashes even more.
tags.boogschutter-stier: One is already gone before the plan exists, the other wants to test-drive twelve options first.
tags.boogschutter-steenbok: Philosopher versus CEO: war in the calendar, peace on the holiday trip.
tags.boogschutter-tweelingen: Two conversation cannons on full automatic: the checkout enjoys listening in, the neighbours don't.
tags.boogschutter-vissen: One leaves for abroad, the other for a daydream. They bump into each other on the way.
tags.boogschutter-waterman: Freedom-loving with their own theory: the discussion lasts longer than the trip itself.
tags.boogschutter-weegschaal: One picks a new continent every day, the other still can't choose breakfast.
tags.kreeft-kreeft: Two home bankers who both know the other still remembers the 2016 argument.
tags.kreeft-leeuw: One wants applause, the other wants understanding. Both get it — if they wait their turn.
tags.kreeft-maagd: Care team complete: one dabs, the other checks whether the dab was antistatic.
tags.kreeft-ram: One kicks the door in, the other cleans up afterwards. A classic in the chaos catalogue.
tags.kreeft-schorpioen: Two water dams with the same filing system: this costs nothing, this archives.
tags.kreeft-stier: Two house pets under one blanket: rarely has a receipt been this calm.
tags.kreeft-steenbok: One tends the nest, the other the mortgage. Rarely falls apart.
tags.kreeft-tweelingen: One talks about every feeling, the other is already on four personas. The checkout just about keeps up.
tags.kreeft-vissen: Two emotional sponges who wring themselves out together once a week.
tags.kreeft-waterman: One wants closeness, the other a concept. 'Distance' shows up on the receipt as a charge.
tags.kreeft-weegschaal: A crying event gets scheduled while the other is still trying to fit it in. Somehow still cosy in the end.
tags.leeuw-leeuw: Two spotlights, one stage: the show is fantastic as long as someone brought an extinguisher.
tags.leeuw-maagd: One wants an audience, the other spots a smudge on the spotlight.
tags.leeuw-ram: Two sparks without brakes: seductive fireworks, fire brigade unfortunately not called.
tags.leeuw-schorpioen: Royal drama in the arena: one wants applause, the other control. Audience guaranteed.
tags.leeuw-stier: One gleams, the other quietly enjoys it from the sofa. Surprisingly stable pairing.
tags.leeuw-steenbok: The show needs a producer: the other arrived with a marketing plan and a budget.
tags.leeuw-tweelingen: Three audiences at once: the real one, the virtual one and the one in their heads. Pleasantly busy, at least.
tags.leeuw-vissen: One looks for the stage, the other for the main character of the play. Nicely matched.
tags.leeuw-waterman: One wants to be adored, the other explains that adoration is a construct. Then adores them anyway.
tags.leeuw-weegschaal: The other always applauds at exactly the right moment, perfectly rehearsed. Show stays on the rails.
tags.maagd-maagd: Two spreadsheets that together produce one perfect postcard of a household.
tags.maagd-ram: One has the plan, the other had already carried it out — and then repaired it themselves.
tags.maagd-schorpioen: One audits the receipt for errors, the other sees the errors that don't exist yet. Efficient pairing.
tags.maagd-stier: Two calm types with a tight schedule and an unbreakable dishwasher-loading technique.
tags.maagd-steenbok: The toothbrush couple of the zodiac: everything by protocol, nobody complains.
tags.maagd-tweelingen: One phrases it perfectly, the other already left the meeting. Fine duo.
tags.maagd-vissen: One clears up the mess, the other saw the mess as art. Good balance on the receipt.
tags.maagd-waterman: One sees the details, the other the system. Together they see everything — and improve nothing too loudly.
tags.maagd-weegschaal: Two weighers sharing one scale, taking turns criticising it.
tags.ram-ram: Two gas turbines without brakes: great on the motorway, life raft forgotten.
tags.ram-schorpioen: Full speed versus deep water — the combination that makes every wrecked evening memorable.
tags.ram-stier: One wants it now, the other wants it in a bit (or, failing that, the day after tomorrow). The till works overtime.
tags.ram-steenbok: Action while the plan still needs writing: the job recognises it, the relationship wears out.
tags.ram-tweelingen: Energy on several fronts at once: nobody knows which front, but there's a lot of fun.
tags.ram-vissen: One storms the roundabout, the other dreams they already left it. Confusingly sweet.
tags.ram-waterman: Two revolutionaries with their own manifesto and one shared printer.
tags.ram-weegschaal: One decides at the first word, the other only once the cutlery is out. Still a dynamic duo.
tags.schorpioen-schorpioen: Two archives full of secrets, each knowing the other hasn't said the worst part yet. Intense, never boring.
tags.schorpioen-stier: Stubborn rock versus stubborn rock: as long as the bridge holds, nobody needs to go under it.
tags.schorpioen-steenbok: Two master plans in one house: whoever plays the better game gets to manage the budget.
tags.schorpioen-tweelingen: Rememberer of everything versus forgetter of eighty percent: a lot of 'what did you say?' — and a lot of saved receipts.
tags.schorpioen-vissen: Two water depths understanding each other without words — and writing a book about each other without saying so.
tags.schorpioen-waterman: Secrets versus opinions: one digs, the other bends around them. Fascinating conversation material.
tags.schorpioen-weegschaal: One weighs the intention, the other the kindness next to it. Sounds fragile, works surprisingly well.
tags.stier-stier: Two fixed anchors who don't need to go anywhere together — perfect for the sofa and the receipt.
tags.stier-tweelingen: Calm rhythm versus ten thoughts a minute: one offers the other a chair, the other offers adventure.
tags.stier-vissen: One handles bed, sofa and broccoli, the other dreams about where the party is.
tags.stier-waterman: One wants the same menu every day, the other a new concept. The food in between? Also nice.
tags.stier-weegschaal: Comfort zone versus style advice: the till calls it a perfect match and the scales stop wavering.
tags.steenbok-steenbok: Two CEOs who could both use a hug, but never quite get around to mentioning it.
tags.steenbok-stier: Two dependable fixtures in one household: one plans the future, the other protects the sofa. Calm, stable, mildly predictable.
tags.steenbok-tweelingen: Structure versus flow: one holds it together, the other loosens it up. Together unbeatable at being restless.
tags.steenbok-vissen: The realistic planner and the dreamer with the loveliest plans. They complete each other's receipts beautifully.
tags.steenbok-waterman: Tradition and revolution, in one tidy mood: they argue about the future, then arrange it together.
tags.steenbok-weegschaal: Both love a clear schedule and a nice frame. A match with tidiness.
tags.tweelingen-tweelingen: The conversation is twice as fast and the decision twice as far away. Would someone like to take notes?

tags.tweelingen-waterman: Two turbo idea machines finishing each other's thoughts halfway through. Outsiders hear only mumbling.
tags.tweelingen-weegschaal: Two waverers who elevate indecision into an art form. Impressively postponed.
tags.vissen-vissen: Two daydreamers in one aquarium: the restaurant owner simply locks the door.
tags.vissen-waterman: One dreams, the other analyses the dream in real time. Quite a nice conversation after midnight.
tags.vissen-weegschaal: One lives life as a film, the other directs a snack along with it. Pleasantly escaping together.
tags.waterman-waterman: Two aliens with their own theory of humanity — and a shared break.
tags.waterman-weegschaal: Discussing the system stylishly instead of doing anything about it: the table is the stage.
